app_info.subtitle: Explore US county maps
app_info.description: Atlas is an atlas of the United States inside ChatGPT. Open any of the 3,222 US counties and see its real outline, its named lakes, bays and rivers, and where its towns actually sit — then zoom out to the state or the whole country. Ask which county a town is in, how large a county is, or what water runs through it, and the answer comes from the 2024 US Census rather than from memory. Atlas is built to be right or to say it does not know: a name that could mean several places returns the list instead of a guess, and a name it does not carry is refused outright. Every map is drawn from public-domain Census TIGERweb geography on an equal-area projection, so counties are shown at honest relative size. Atlas has no accounts, no payments, and no advertising, and it does not track you.

commerce.notes: Atlas has no commerce surface of any kind. It exposes no checkout, no paid tier, no subscription, and no link out to any purchase flow. Both tools are read-only reads of public-domain US Census data.

starter_prompts: Show me Riverside County on a map.
What county is Eastvale, CA in?
Open Miami-Dade County and tell me what water is in it.
Show me the whole United States by county.
plugin_submission.release_notes: First release. Atlas draws all 3,222 US counties from public-domain Census TIGERweb geography on an Albers equal-area projection, with named water, 21,155 Census town positions, and a nation to state to county zoom. A county opens in context, with its neighbours running off the edge of the plate. Two read-only tools: open a place on the map with its Census facts, and look up which places carry a given name. Place resolution is gated by an automated battery requiring zero confidently-wrong answers across 1,472 cases; ambiguous names return candidates and unknown names are refused.

justifications.read_only_justification: Resolves a place name against a local Census index, returns a reference to a map plate for the widget to draw, and returns that county's Census facts (land area, largest places, named water). It creates and changes nothing, and repeating the same call returns the same result.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only Census geography files bundled with the server. It makes no third-party request, publishes nothing, and contacts no external system.
justifications.destructive_justification: Cannot delete, overwrite, revoke access, charge money, send a message, or take any action with an effect outside the conversation.

justifications.read_only_justification: Looks a name up in a static index of 21,155 Census places and 3,222 counties and returns matching entries. Nothing is written and the same query always returns the same entries.
justifications.open_world_justification: Searches a local dataset only. No search engine, no geocoding provider, no network call leaves the server.
justifications.destructive_justification: Returns index entries and nothing else. It has no capability to modify, delete, send, or purchase.

test_cases.user_prompt: Show me Riverside County, California on a map.
test_cases.expected_output: Opens Riverside County with its real Census boundary and town positions, and states that this county's streets are not mapped.
test_cases.fixture_data: No login. Uses bundled Census geography for riverside-ca.

test_cases.description: Look up which county a town is in.
test_cases.user_prompt: What county is Eastvale, CA in?
test_cases.expected_output: Answers that Eastvale is in Riverside County, California, from the Census place index.
test_cases.fixture_data: No login. Uses the bundled Census place index.

test_cases.description: Open a county and get its Census facts with the map.
test_cases.user_prompt: How big is Miami-Dade County and what water is in it?
test_cases.expected_output: Opens Miami-Dade and reports roughly 1,900 square miles of land, its largest Census places, and named water such as Florida Bay.
test_cases.fixture_data: No login. Uses bundled Census geography for miami-dade-fl.

test_cases.description: Refuse to guess an ambiguous place name.
test_cases.expected_output: Does not open a map. Returns the real Springfields with their states and counties, and asks which one was meant.
test_cases.fixture_data: No login. Springfield exists in many states in the Census index.

test_cases.description: Zoom out to the national map.
test_cases.user_prompt: Show me the whole United States by county.
test_cases.expected_output: Opens the national plate with all 3,222 counties and state boundaries, with Alaska, Hawaii and Puerto Rico drawn as labelled insets.
test_cases.fixture_data: No login. Uses the prebuilt national plate.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not answer for a place Atlas does not carry.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Show me Paris, France on the map.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Atlas covers United States counties only and says so. It must not open a US place with a similar name in its place.
negative_test_cases.why_not_complete: Atlas is a US Census atlas; it holds no geography outside the United States.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not act as a navigation or local search product.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Give me driving directions to the nearest open pharmacy and how long it takes.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app is not invoked. Atlas has no routing, no travel times, and no business listings, and says the data is not in Atlas.
negative_test_cases.why_not_complete: Atlas draws county geography. It carries no roads-level routing, no opening hours, and no places of business.

negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Sign me up for Atlas Pro and charge my card.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: No tool is called. Atlas has no account, no paid tier and no checkout, and states this plainly.
negative_test_cases.why_not_complete: Atlas exposes no commerce surface at all; there is no payment tool to call and no restricted payment data may be collected.
